metadata.description: Every repository's services, one entry per service
notes: A repository is looked up here by its name ("repository"); its calling workflow needs no services file of its own
One entry for a repository deploys as a polyrepo under the entry's "name"; several deploy as a monorepo
"name" is what a service deploys as (the <name>-<domain> values key and image)
requires lists the platform services it needs; their wiring is in the GitOps values and ExternalSecrets
"repositories" holds a repository's defaults, merged under each of its entries; an entry's own fields win, and "version" merges key by key
Build options per entry or repository: project_type, service_type, version {dotnet, node}, directory, nx_project (defaults to name), dockerfile, docker_target, environments

services.name: airlinegds
services.notes: The GDS API over Crane and Videcom; its Dockerfile's api stage. Staging runs the sandbox deployment

services.name: gateway
services.notes: The YARP entry point, on its own host gateway.exampleorg.dev

services.name: adminapi
services.notes: Admin, notification and audit in one host; adminapi because admin-exampleorg-dev is the admin frontend

services.name: paymentgateway
services.notes: Payment providers behind one contract; webhooks off in staging

services.name: booking
services.notes: The gateway's /flights and /hotels; its own PostgreSQL database, migrated at startup

services.name: vas
services.notes: The gateway's /vas; every purchase off by default

services.name: hotelgds
services.notes: booking's /hotels/v1 (sandbox in staging); one replica: bookings are in memory

services.name: external-gateway
services.notes: The agencies' entry point: api.<domain>/flights and /hotels, forwarded to booking after identity checks the key

services.name: wallet
services.notes: Replaces wallet.api through staged switches; its staging entry stays disabled until then
